items.text: Hey all, just a small patch to address a couple of issues that have been flagged since v2.0.
Some text strings in the Japanese localization were muddled, these have now been fixed and should be displaying the correct text where needed.
The invert third person camera toggle was previously not working for the beginning section with Sasha on the beach. This has now been fixed too.

I am aware of some performance issues that have cropped up in v2.0 in exterior locations when playing on Steam Deck. I'm still working out what has caused this but will push another patch when I have a solution. For the time being, enabling half rate shading on the Steam Deck performance settings should give a decent boost to FPS.

Hey all, we have another update! The star of the show this time is the new fully featured third person mode. A much requested feature that I finally worked out a way to implement without breaking the traditional camera system.

The game will now offer the player two options regarding camera style when starting the game 'Classic' and 'Modern' these represent the original fixed camera mode and the new third person camera, this option can of course be switched at any time during gameplay from the Options menu.

Along with this new camera system I have put a lot of time into optimising aspects of the game that I felt were lacking alongside some improvements and balancing to combat and enemies. I have also made some significant changes to how the game handles loading of data, fixing issues with black screens during loading of save files and new areas.

Hopefully the game should feel a lot smoother now thanks to many small updates across the board. As always I'd love to hear your thoughts or any issues you may run into over in the Steam discussion forums.

Please note: Whilst I have tried my best to avoid breaking any previous save data when updating to Patch 9, due to the nature of the improvements in this update some issues may arise from loading old save files. I recommend starting a New Game save file where possible.

Hi all, I hope you've been enjoying the updates to Hollowbody since release.

Since the game's release I have been focussing on improving technical aspects of Hollowbody and fixing various bugs based on community feedback. Over the past weeks I took some time to reflect on more general feedback, in particular taking note of game pacing and narrative aspects that didn't quite hit the mark for everyone.

During this period of refection I looked back at my original design notes for Hollowbody and some of the aspects of the game that were cut due to time constraints and various other influences. There came a point in development where I had to really lock-in the game structure and focus on the core design work that would see Hollowbody through to release. Whilst I am very happy with how Hollowbody released and the fantastic reception it's received from players, there were some narrative threads missing from the game that contextualize Echo's place in the grand scheme of Hollowbody's story.

This update looks to remedy that. Alongside some additional interactions and puzzle sections added to the later stages of the game I've been working on a larger optional puzzle that spans several locations, with the solution hopefully clearing up some confusion players had about the city's restoration efforts and subsequent downfall. Keep an eye out for new inventory items or changes in the environment.

notes.title: VSync in Graphics Options now has three options

items.text: Uncapped - Allow the game to run without a FPS limit.
Target: Monitor Refresh Rate - The game will aim to lock FPS at your monitor's current refresh rate.
Target: Half Monitor Refresh Rate - The game will aim to lock FPS at half of your monitor's current refresh rate.
If for example you have a 120Hz monitor, setting VSync to 'Target: Half Monitor Refresh Rate' will cause the game to cap at 60FPS.
I recommend capping to either your monitor's refresh rate or half if you're experience heavy GPU load.
Hopefully that clears things up!
